title: Activation-compensation INT8 pipeline and runtime kernel shims
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an end-to-end activation-aware INT8 (SmoothQuant-style) workflow that ties offline calibration and profile generation into the runtime kernel selection path. Deliverables: a calibration job that produces per-layer activation scale profiles, a calibration-to-runtime asset format, lightweight kernel shims that apply activation compensation at inference time, runtime selector rules to prefer compensated fused kernels, and validation/telemetry for accuracy regressions and perf impact.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration job runs as a batch job and emits profile artifacts (JSON) with per-tensor activation scale factors and metadata
Runtime accepts profile artifact and enables activation compensation without requiring model graph rewrites
Kernel shims integrate with the existing kernel selector and add <5% median latency overhead on standard 2048-seqlen workloads
End-to-end accuracy regression <= 1.0% measured on our calibration+validation prompt suite compared to FP16 baseline
CI includes a validation job that verifies no regression on a holdout eval set before merging runtime changes
Fallback behavior: if profile missing or incompatible, runtime falls back to current INT8 kernels with no compensation and emits a clear telemetry flag
technical_notes: Approach: build a two-stage pipeline. (1) Offline collector: run representative inference traces to gather activation histograms and max/mean stats. Compute SmoothQuant-like activation scales using per-channel weight norms and activation variance heuristics; store final per-tensor multiplicative compensation factors. (2) Runtime: implement kernel shims that apply pre-multiply to inputs or post-scale to outputs as required by each fused kernel. We will not rewrite model graphs; instead, provide a lightweight layer at the kernel boundary to apply scales. Add a compact profile spec (versioned) with model-hash, layer-paths, tensor-shapes, dtype targets, and recommended quant params. Kernel integration: add 'compensated_gemm' and 'compensated_conv' entry points that perform scale-apply, call existing int8 kernels, then inverse-scale as needed. Ensure KV-cache and prefix caching paths preserve scales. Telemetry: emit metrics quant.profile.loaded, quant.compensation.applied, quant.accuracy_regression_pct, and a per-request tag quant.profile.id
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype collector that runs on a few representative models and computes scale maps (2d conv, mha, linear) - 1 week
Calibration API: batch job + CLI to run representative traces and upload profile to artifact store - 1 week
Profile format: finalize JSON schema and versioning with backward compatibility notes - 2 days
Runtime shim: implement kernel adapter layer and opt-in config flag - 2 weeks
Kernel fuses: add compensated_fused GEMM/Conv hooks to kernel registry and implement minimal fused kernels - 1 week
Validation harness: add automated accuracy + perf runs to CI and a dashboard for visual diffing - 4 days
Rollout: start canary on dedicated hosts with automatic fallback and monitoring - 3 days
benchmarks: Baseline FP16 throughput/latency captured for bert-large and Llama-13B - bench IDs: bench/2026-01/bert-large, bench/2026-01/llama-13b
Preliminary prototype increased tail latency by ~6-8% on small batch sizes; target <5% after kernel fusion
Preliminary accuracy delta observed: 0.7% average discrepancy on NLU prompts after compensation vs FP16
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete. Collected activation histograms from 5 representative models using sample traces. Initial scale computation script (smooth_comp.py) exists in prototypes/quant/.
2026-02-27: Design review with runtime and kernels; agreed on non-invasive shim approach to avoid graph rewrites. Decided to version profile JSON as v1 with optional per-channel entries.

qa_plan: Create a CI job that runs a small holdout eval suite (200 prompts) at merge time. The job will compare outputs using log-prob and semantic similarity thresholds. If accuracy regression >1.0% or any functional mismatch, mark the job failed. Also run perf microbench for median/95th latency deltas.
rollout_plan: Feature gated by runtime config flag quant.activation_compensation. Rollout steps: (1) internal dev hosts, (2) Canary on dedicated capacity with 5% traffic, (3) expand to non-critical customers, (4) default on for new deployments after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Provide immediate rollback by disabling flag.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: activation compensation may interact poorly with KV cache leading to stale scaling in long-form generation. Mitigation: attach profile version to cached entries and invalidate cache on mismatched profile; implement transparent fallback. Risk: calibration drift across datasets. Mitigation: collect dataset fingerprint and surface recommended dataset for calibration in profile metadata.
notes_for_oncall: If quant.profile.loaded spikes in errors or quant.compensation.applied is 0 despite profile present, check compatibility matrix (model-hash vs profile.model_hash) and S3 access. If accuracy_regression_pct > 2% on canary, immediately disable the compensation flag and open an incident.
